name: CapCut SRT Number Count-Up
use_when: A short-form edit needs a number, price, metric, subscriber count, score, or result to count upward quickly.
The agent can generate or receive an SRT sequence of number captions.
The final number should hold long enough for the viewer to understand the value.
avoid_when: The number is evidence-critical and the animation could misrepresent the data.
The generated SRT contains incorrect, missing, or duplicated values.
The counter would cover proof, product UI, captions, or the subject's face.

timeline_pattern.pattern: generate_number_srt -> import_srt -> apply_font_size_position_to_all -> compound_number_captions -> speed_curve -> extend_final_value_hold -> optional_nested_compound_speedup
timeline_pattern.data_rule: The final value and any currency/unit symbols must be verified before styling.
timeline_pattern.speed_rule: Use a slow-fast-slow curve so the counter starts readable, accelerates, then lands on the final value.
timeline_pattern.hold_rule: Extend the final number inside the compound when the final value needs to remain onscreen.

motion.rule: The count animation should accelerate for energy and decelerate before the final value so the result is readable.

keyframe_values.srt_shape: Each SRT caption is a number step; apply style to all before compounding.
keyframe_values.curve: Use a custom speed curve that starts slow, climbs quickly, then slows near the final number.
keyframe_values.nested_speed: If the number range is large and still too slow, compound the compound and speed the wrapper up again.
keyframe_values.final_hold: Extend the final SRT caption value inside the compound, then extend the compound on the main timeline.

sound.rule: Small ticks can support the count only if they do not mask speech or turn the counter into clutter.

captions.rule: Do not let the number SRT replace accessibility captions unless it is the actual spoken content.

color.rule: Counter text should contrast clearly over the footage and avoid colors that imply unsupported gain/loss meaning.

implementation.ffmpeg: Generate an ASS/SRT counter sequence with verified values, burn it as timed subtitles, and use setpts or segment timing to control speed; hold the final subtitle longer.
implementation.remotion: Generate frame-based number interpolation with verified start/end values, easing, prefix/suffix, and finalHoldFrames instead of depending on SRT.
implementation.blender: Animate a text object's numeric value through drivers or keyframed text strips, then hold the final value.
implementation.capcut_equivalent: Generate or import a numbers SRT, drag it into the timeline, select Apply To All, set font/size/position, create a compound clip, apply a custom speed curve that starts slow, accelerates, and slows at the end, then extend the final value inside the compound.
implementation.premiere_equivalent: Import SRT or use Essential Graphics/MOGRT counter text; nest the number sequence, time-remap for slow-fast-slow motion, and hold the final value.

common_mistakes: Using generated numbers without checking the final value and units.
Speeding the counter so fast that the final number is missed.
Forgetting to hold the final value.
Letting the number counter cover proof, product UI, or ordinary captions.
Animating a metric in a way that exaggerates or misrepresents the real data.
qc: Is the final number, currency, unit, or label correct?
Does the counter slow or hold long enough for the final value to read?
Does the counter avoid faces, captions, product UI, and proof?
Do ticks or SFX stay below speech if used?
Is the animation truthful to the data being shown?
